pr_title: Fix nest streams that get stuck broken
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove line that sets the stream to unavailable, which was added accidentally in a bad merge. The original behavior in #62294  is correct and #61647 added this incorrectly.

Nest streams are often flaky (e.g. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/60353) on initial connection, then they get stuck, and this helps resolve that. Once marked unavailable, none of the frontend stream attributes are set, making the player in the frontend ineffective at performing retries. The stream available=False may only be set when keepalive is true, otherwise it will never attempt to be marked available again by the stream worker. In the future we can update retry behavior so that we can also use unavailable for non-keepalive streams, but it needs more work either in frontend or in. stream worker.

Let me see if I can explain what i think we're seeing:

- Nest cams generally have an issue where they throw 404s for some reason e.g. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/60353 and other developers see this also https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70086032/rtsp-streams-often-fail-with-404-on-describe-method -- its not specific to home assistant.
- In 2022.2 I changed the behavior for all streams as part of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/54659 so that when a `Preload stream` is **retrying in the worker**, it is now marked unavailable.  The previous behavior is that the frontend would not tell you there was a problem it it would either show you a frozen image or it would show a spinning video icon
- There was a bug where that would happen even if it was not retrying. When marked unavailable, you could never get out of that state ever again. (Fixed in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/60353)

Hi @allenporter, I still am seeing that the 2020.12.10 version behaviour is quite different from the 2021.02.x versions. On the old version, I would rarely get blank images (camera.snapshot) or recordings (camera.record), but they did happen intermittently (one failure every two weeks). Would the "unavailable" state affect snapshot and record?

Yes, we're explicitly marking the camera unavailable now when the stream itself is broken as requested in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/54659 to have "correct" error handling, which seems to turn off some things for the entity (e.g. stream won't render)

The way this works today is we have two processes going:
- worker stream: background thread opening the rtsp stream and reading everything
- snapshot image: opens the rtsp image again and connects to the stream

I think part of the reason why the stream is getting a 404 may be because the stream is being opened twice, once by the snapshot and once by the worker. I have a theory that using a `Picture Glance Card` with `live` may be less likely to get a 404 since the stream is only used once, even though it may happen from time to time still.  I'm actively updating the code to not make both of these requests and to always just use the last image from the worker stream https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/66427
